text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Nigeria's Olympics soccer team captain 20-year-old Nwankwo Kano survives heart surgery in the United States.
- Forex demand at weekly auction drops to $23.67 million from $26.67 million last week.
- Non-oil exports up in July, August and September 1996, a departure from the lull in April, says chamber of commerce.
- Shell oil company says Nigeria needs to pay $5 billion to end gas flaring.
- Police link opposition group to car bomb explosion two weeks ago which killed three persons; says one of the three was agent of NALICON led by exiled Nobel laureate Wole Soyinka.
- Central bank orders that all distressed banks should henceforth not collect deposits from customers.
- Chief anti-narcotics officer Major-General Musa Bamaiyi says bankers are not cooperating enough in the battle against money laundering.
- Coca-Cola bottlers, Nigerian Bottling Company, says it will introduce low-priced drinks next year and expects its turnover to rise to 19 billion naira.
- Nigeria Airways plane seized in London over debt owed to a British firm has been released, flies home on Friday.
- The seven African producers of gum arabic set to form export cartel after meeting in Lagos on Friday.
